record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Are there infinite additive-cube-free words on the following alphabets: {0, 1, 2, 3}, {0, 1, 4} and {0, 2, 5}?

evidence.quote: Are there infinite additive-cube-free words on the following alphabets: {0, 1, 2, 3}, {0, 1, 4} and {0, 2, 5}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite subset of the integers. A finite word w = a_1 a_2 ... a_n with letters in A is called an additive cube if it can be partitioned into three consecutive nonempty blocks of equal length whose letter-sums coincide; that is, there exist indices 0 = i_0 < i_1 < i_2 < i_3 = n with i_1 - i_0 = i_2 - i_1 = i_3 - i_2 such that
  sum_{j=i_0+1}^{i_1} a_j = sum_{j=i_1+1}^{i_2} a_j = sum_{j=i_2+1}^{i_3} a_j.
An infinite word over A is called additive-cube-free if none of its finite factors is an additive cube.

Determine, for each of the following alphabets A, whether there exists an infinite additive-cube-free word over A:
(a) A = {0, 1, 2, 3};
(b) A = {0, 1, 4};
(c) A = {0, 2, 5}.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (Rao and Rosenfeld, "Avoidability of Additive Cubes over Alphabets of Four Numbers") established that infinite additive-cube-free words exist over every 3-letter integer alphabet not equivalent to a single point, including {0,1,4} and {0,2,5}, and over every 4-letter alphabet except possibly {0,1,2,3}. The case A = {0,1,2,3} is explicitly left open: it is known only that additive-cube-free words of length > 10^8 exist over {0,1,2,3}, but the existence of an infinite such word remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of Additive Cubes over Alphabets of Four Numbers
status_evidence.snippet: We leave the case of {0,1,2,3} open... additive cubes are avoidable over alphabets of size 4 not equivalent to {0,1,2,3}.
status_evidence.claim: {0,1,4} and {0,2,5} are resolved affirmatively; {0,1,2,3} remains open.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding abelian and additive powers in rich words
status_evidence.snippet: Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer, and Shallit constructed an infinite additive cube-free word over {0,1,3,4}; later extensions cover further alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: Background on existence of infinite additive cube-free words over various integer alphabets.
